# RecSys-Industrial-Book

> Reader and Agent entry point for *推荐系统：工业架构与核心算法*.

## Authoritative content

- Book content is distributed as released chapter PDFs in the `chNN 章节名/` directories.
- This repository intentionally does not publish LaTeX, extracted PDF text, or a prose-equivalent Markdown edition.
- `llms.txt` is a concise project/topic index, not the book text.

## Agent workflows

- Canonical policy: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)
- Claude Code entry: [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md)
- Reader setup and privacy boundary: [docs/agent-guide.md](docs/agent-guide.md)
- Q&A Skill: [.claude/skills/recsys-book-qa/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/recsys-book-qa/SKILL.md)
- Engineering Skill: [.claude/skills/recsys-engineering/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/recsys-engineering/SKILL.md)

## Local commands

```bash
python3 tools/recsys_agent.py index
python3 tools/recsys_agent.py search "双塔召回 负采样偏差"
python3 templates/recommendation-pipeline/app.py --user u1 --limit 5
python3 -m unittest discover -s templates/recommendation-pipeline/tests -v
python3 tools/check_public_boundary.py
```

The generated `.recsys-agent/` directory is a disposable, ignored local cache. Cite the source PDF and PDF page in book-grounded answers.

## Knowledge map

The released PDFs cover the industrial recommendation pipeline, including system architecture, recall/filtering, pre-ranking, ranking, re-ranking, mixed ranking, generative recommendation, retrieval models, feature engineering, offline/online services, vector retrieval, bias, duration modeling, and reinforcement-learning recommendation. The set grows as chapters are released; inspect repository chapter directories for current availability.

## Coding boundary

Repository code has three intended levels:

1. chapter examples for explaining algorithms;
2. reference implementations with runnable behavior;
3. `templates/` as Agent starting points for complete engineering slices.

Teaching mocks are not production integrations. Agent-generated designs must still resolve workload, latency, consistency, availability, deployment, privacy, and cost constraints.
